title: The disrupted navigational compass: pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical interventions for spatial navigation deficits
title_zh: 受累的导航指南针：空间导航缺陷的病理生理机制与临床干预
abstract: Spatial navigation is a higher-order integrative cognitive ability that supports environmental orientation, goal-directed route selection, and adaptive locomotion by integrating spatial memory, multisensory cues, attention, and executive control. Neural systems supporting navigation are also vulnerable to aging and neurodegenerative disease, making navigation a useful domain for linking basic mechanisms with clinically measurable functional impairment. This review summarizes spatial-navigation mechanisms across multiple levels. At the cognitive level, navigation depends on interacting processes including spatial representation, path integration, reference-frame transformation, landmark use, and route planning. At the network level, hippocampal-entorhinal, retrosplenial-parietal, scene-selective, and prefrontal systems contribute complementary functions. At the cellular level, place-, grid-, head-direction-, speed-, and boundary-related representations encode position, heading, self-motion, environmental geometry, and prospective behavior. Clinical and neuroimaging studies indicate that navigation impairment is associated with structural and functional abnormalities, with the strongest diagnostic evidence currently arising from Alzheimer's disease and its prodromal stages. VR-based behavioral assessment and electrophysiological approaches provide complementary means of characterizing navigation phenotypes: VR enables controlled, repeatable, process-sensitive tasks, whereas intracranial and scalp recordings provide neural information at different spatial and physiological scales. No pharmacological agent has been developed or licensed specifically for navigation impairment; current navigation-focused interventions therefore rely mainly on behavioral and VR-based rehabilitation, compensatory strategies, and emerging neuromodulation approaches. Future studies should integrate process-specific behavioral and physiological markers with biomarker-defined clinical cohorts, and use large, randomized, longitudinal studies to establish diagnostic validity, real-world transfer, and mechanism-informed intervention effects.
abstract_zh: 空间导航是一种高阶整合性认知能力，通过整合空间记忆、多感觉线索、注意与执行控制，支持环境定位、目标导向的路线选择及适应性运动。支撑导航的神经系统同样易受衰老与神经退行性疾病影响，因此导航成为连接基础机制与临床可测功能损害的有用领域。本综述从多个层面总结空间导航机制。在认知层面，导航依赖于包括空间表征、路径积分、参照系变换、地标使用及路径规划在内的相互作用过程。在网络层面，海马-内嗅、回扣-顶叶、场景选择性及前额叶系统贡献互补功能。在细胞层面，位置细胞、栅格细胞、头向细胞、速度细胞及边界相关表征对位置、航向、自身运动、环境几何及预期行为进行编码。临床与神经影像学研究表明，导航障碍与结构及功能异常相关，目前最强的诊断证据来自阿尔茨海默病及其前驱期。基于虚拟现实的行为评估与电生理方法提供了刻画导航表型的互补手段：虚拟现实可实现受控、可重复且对过程敏感的任务，而颅内及头皮记录则在不同空间与生理尺度提供神经信息。目前尚无专为导航障碍开发或批准的药物；因此，以导航为重点的干预主要依赖行为与虚拟现实康复、代偿策略及新兴的神经调节方法。未来研究应将过程特异的行为与生理标志物与生物标志物定义的临床队列相结合，并开展大规模、随机、纵向研究，以确立诊断效度、现实世界迁移及基于机制的干预效应。
